proposals.before: In the fifth month, on jichou, he seized Sizhou, paid homage at the ancestral tombs, and offered his father’s spirit an old ox and wine.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, on jichou, he seized Sizhou, paid homage at the ancestral tombs, and bestowed oxen and wine on the local elders.
proposals.reason: Chinese 賜父老牛酒 means he bestowed oxen and wine on the elders (父老), not an offering to his father’s spirit.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, on the jichou day, he took Sizhou, visited the imperial tombs, and bestowed an old ox and wine on his father.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, on the jichou day, he took Sizhou, visited the imperial tombs, and bestowed oxen and wine on the elders.
proposals.reason: 父老 denotes local elders/commoner elders, not ‘his father’.

proposals.before: On yichou he came to Jinchuan Gate. The Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gates and let him in. The capital fell that day.
proposals.after: On yichou he came to Jinchuan Gate. The Prince of Gu, Zhu Hui, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gates and let him in. The capital fell that day.
proposals.reason: Chinese personal name is 橞 (Hui), not Yunyi; the English given name mismatches the Chinese.

proposals.before: On the yichou day, he reached Jinchuan Gate; the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gate and admitted the Prince; the capital city then fell.
proposals.after: On the yichou day, he reached Jinchuan Gate; the Prince of Gu Zhu Hui, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gate and admitted the Prince; the capital city then fell.
proposals.reason: Chinese 橞 is Hui; Yunyi is a mistranslation of the given name.

proposals.before: On renshen the Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, was moved to a new fief at Changsha.
proposals.after: On renshen the Prince of Gu, Zhu Hui, was moved to a new fief at Changsha.
proposals.reason: Chinese 橞 corresponds to Hui, not Yunyi.

proposals.before: On the renshen day, the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi was transferred in enfeoffment to Changsha.
proposals.after: On the renshen day, the Prince of Gu Zhu Hui was transferred in enfeoffment to Changsha.
proposals.reason: Chinese 橞 is Hui; Yunyi is incorrect.

decisions.reason: s0157 賜父老牛酒 means he bestowed oxen and wine on the elders (父老); the original misreads 父老 as an offering to his father’s spirit and attaches 老 to 牛.
父老 is the fixed compound for local elders, not ‘his father’; 牛酒 is oxen and wine as a gift, so the literal’s ‘old ox … on his father’ is wrong.
s0172 names 谷王橞; 橞 is Hui (Zhu Hui). Zhu Yunyi is not supported by the Chinese personal name.
The literal must render 橞 as Hui; Yunyi invents a different given name not present in 谷王橞.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 谷王橞、李景隆等开門納王

decisions.reason: s0208 again has 谷王橞; the personal name is Hui, so Zhu Yunyi must be corrected to Zhu Hui.
Literal 谷王橞 requires Zhu Hui; Yunyi is an English mistranslation of the same given name 橞.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows Zhu Yunyi was invented solely by mistranslating 橞; s0172 supports the personal name Hui (橞), not an alternate Yunyi.
